definition: In computer vision, the term cuboid is used to describe a small spatiotemporal volume extracted for purposes of behavior recognition.
details: The cuboid is regarded as a basic geometric primitive type and is used to depict three-dimensional objects within a three dimensional representation of a flat, two dimensional image.

explainer.lead: In computer vision, a cuboid is a small block of visual data with width, height, and duration. It lets a system examine what happens in one part of a scene over a short time, which is useful for recognizing behavior.

tiers.eli5: Imagine cutting a tiny rectangular piece out of a video, keeping several moments rather than just one picture. That piece is like a small box: it covers part of the picture and a short stretch of time. A computer can study it to help understand an action.
tiers.practitioner: Use a cuboid as a spatiotemporal patch defined by its image position, spatial size, and temporal extent. Its contents can then be described and supplied to a behavior-recognition process. The patch captures only its selected region and time span, so placement and extent determine what evidence is available.
tiers.paperLevel: For video coordinates (x, y, t), a cuboid can be written as C = [x, x + w) × [y, y + h) × [t, t + d), where w and h are spatial dimensions and d is duration. It is a finite spatiotemporal volume used for behavior recognition; the term also denotes a geometric primitive for depicting three-dimensional objects. The definition alone does not specify a feature descriptor or recognition method.

explainer.example: In a video of a person raising a hand, select a rectangle around the hand and keep it over the frames covering the beginning of the movement. The resulting block is a spatiotemporal cuboid containing both the hand's appearance and its change over that interval.

usedIn.name: Behavior recognition
usedIn.detail: Small spatiotemporal volumes provide localized visual evidence across time.

usedIn.name: Three-dimensional object representation
usedIn.detail: Cuboids serve as basic geometric primitives for depicting objects in a 3D interpretation of a flat image.

explainer.intuition: A single image rectangle shows where something is, while a cuboid also preserves a short interval in which it changes. The same box shape can also act as a simple primitive for representing a three-dimensional object.
howItWorks: Start with video frames arranged in space and time.
Choose a small rectangular image region.
Keep that region across a short sequence of frames.
Treat the resulting width-by-height-by-time block as a cuboid.
Use its contents as input to behavior recognition.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a simple unit for analyzing local appearance together with temporal change. It also connects video analysis with the broader use of cuboids as simple 3D geometric primitives.
misconceptions: A cuboid is a volume of data or a geometric primitive, not a complete recognition algorithm.
A spatiotemporal cuboid includes time, unlike an ordinary rectangle in one image.
It need not contain an entire object or action.

diagram.caption: A spatial region and a time interval together define a cuboid extracted from video.
